situation: Tenant reported weeds, overgrown hedge and an uncleared strip in the communal garden; the system gate says landlord approval must come first.
boundaries: No landlord approval yet for any attendance or works
Communal areas may be handled by the landlord's own contractor
happened: event 4: emailed the landlord the tenant's report and asked how they want to respond.

situation: Landlord replied that he met his own contractor (Riverside) on site and is awaiting quotes, and will follow up on Monday.
boundaries: Landlord is arranging his own contractor; the agency has no quote to approve
Landlord said he will follow up Monday; do not chase before then
happened: event 8: put on hold waiting for the landlord, to follow up Monday.
note: Telling the tenant the landlord is getting quotes is also reasonable; the agency did not update the tenant until 5 Nov.

situation: Landlord promised to follow up on Monday 13 Oct about his contractor's quotes; nothing heard by 16 Oct.
boundaries: Landlord has not yet received or approved any quote
happened: event 9: emailed the landlord asking whether Riverside's quote had arrived.

situation: Landlord confirmed he has his contractor's quotes and agreed to go ahead with the garden works using his own contractor.
boundaries: Landlord is managing his own contractor; the agency does not instruct or pay them
No start date has been given yet
happened: events 23-25: thanked the landlord and asked for the start date, then told the tenant a contractor had been instructed and a date would follow.

situation: The landlord's contractor started the large communal job around 20 Nov (it was delayed by nesting pigeons); by 10 Dec nobody has confirmed completion.
boundaries: Nobody has confirmed the job is finished
The contractor was hired by the landlord, not the agency
happened: event 39: called the contractor (Freya) for an update and left a callback number.

situation: In a phone call the contractor confirmed the job, including the tree removal, is complete and discussed invoicing; the landlord pays the contractor directly.
boundaries: The contractor confirmed completion by phone; neither the tenant nor the landlord has confirmed it in writing
The landlord pays the contractor directly; the agency has no invoice to process
happened: events 43-44: noted that the job was done and the landlord pays directly; closed without payment.

situation: Tenant reports a blocked toilet with a blockage lodged at the pan connector, needing the toilet removed.
boundaries: No landlord approval or standing consent recorded yet
happened: events 2-3: got the landlord's approval by phone to send a contractor, then rang the contractor.
note: If standing consent existed, contractor.assign would be fine, but none is shown at this point.

situation: The contractor visited on 8 Aug; by 12 Aug no work report has come in and the system flags 'no work results'.
boundaries: Visit took place but no outcome reported
No quote received yet
happened: the contractor's report and quote arrived at event 16 (same minute as the system prompt at event 15).

situation: Contractor attended and reports the toilet needs repiping; removal risks breaking it (rusted screws, no spare), so he quotes for a new toilet and cistern, with photos.
boundaries: Landlord approved attendance, not this replacement quote
happened: event 17: emailed the quote and photos to the landlord for approval.

situation: The landlord replied 'Please approve this quote for works.'
boundaries: Approval covers the quoted new toilet and cistern only
happened: events 21-24: recorded the approval, told the tenant the contractor would book in, and told the contractor to schedule the work and send before/after photos and the invoice.

situation: The replacement was booked for 15 Aug, and on 19 Aug the contractor confirmed the job complete, attaching a completion image and invoice.
boundaries: The contractor says it is done; the tenant has not confirmed
The invoice and image are referenced but not readable in the record
happened: events 35-40: marked complete, skipped the document upload, and closed after checks.
note: Forwarding the invoice to the landlord before closing is the better close-out; the record shows no landlord email.

situation: The request is already closed after checks, but the system auto-paused it for an exceeded deadline and it keeps reappearing on the dashboard.
boundaries: The work is done and closed; the auto-pause is a system artefact, not a new issue
happened: events 44-49: raised the system issue internally on Slack, held it, attached the invoice, and a supervisor completed it.
note: Noise moment: the stale automated alert should not trigger any outbound message.

situation: Agency-raised request after checkout: get an estimate for an end-of-tenancy clean, removal of dumped items and a carpet clean; the property is empty.
boundaries: Asking for an estimate is not approval to do the work
The tenant has vacated; there is nobody to arrange access with
happened: events 2-4: assigned a cleaner and emailed the estimate request with the checkout report.

situation: The cleaner replied 'Please tell me if it didn't attach', which implies an estimate was sent, but its contents are not visible.
boundaries: The estimate amount is not visible in the record
Agency receipt of an estimate is not landlord approval
happened: events 8-10: told the cleaner 'Received, please proceed' and noted 'Estimate approved' with no landlord approval recorded.
note: The agency approved the estimate itself. Unless standing consent covers checkout cleans, a good agent sends it to the landlord (or confirms the attachment arrived) before instructing. The final invoice was £125.

situation: The cleaner has been told to proceed and replied 'Lovely thankyou'.
boundaries: An acknowledgement is not completion
happened: event 15: put on hold waiting for the provider.
note: Noise moment: the acknowledgement needs no reply.

situation: The cleaner says the invoice has been sent to the agency (the invoice lists the end-of-tenancy clean, carpet shampoo and removal of dumped items; £125).
boundaries: Completion is evidenced only by the cleaner's invoice; there are no photos
happened: events 18-22: marked complete, emailed the invoice to the landlord and closed the request.

situation: Agency-raised quote request for a checkout clean (vacuum, light clean, limescale in the en-suite); the gate says landlord approval is confirmed, but the system paused the job as 'NOT TENANTED'.
boundaries: The NOT TENANTED pause is expected for a checkout job; it is not a blocker
A quote request is not approval of works
happened: events 5-6: emailed the cleaner asking for a quote, with the checkout report attached.

situation: The cleaner confirms the quote has been sent.
boundaries: The landlord has not approved this quote
happened: event 10: emailed the quote to the landlord asking whether the cleaner may proceed.

situation: The landlord replied 'Pls go ahead' to the cleaning quote.
boundaries: Approval covers the quoted clean only
happened: events 13-16: told the landlord the clean will happen after the checkout works; told the cleaner the quote is approved but to wait for the checkout works to finish.

situation: The cleaner was told the quote is approved and to wait for the checkout works; the cleaner replied 'Thankyou xx'.
boundaries: An acknowledgement is not completion
happened: event 18: put on hold to follow up once the checkout works were done.
note: Noise moment: the acknowledgement needs no reply.

situation: The cleaner confirmed she would attend on the Friday after the checkout works; the agency has heard nothing since about completion or an invoice.
boundaries: No completion confirmation yet
happened: event 34: emailed the cleaner asking whether the clean is done and for the invoice.

situation: The cleaner confirms the job is complete and the invoice is sent.
boundaries: No before/after photos; completion rests on the cleaner's word
happened: events 37-42: forwarded the invoice to the landlord, skipped the photo upload, and closed.

situation: After the tenant vacated, the agency wants an estimate for a full clean, including appliances, freezer defrost and a carpet clean in bedroom two; the system paused the job as NOT TENANTED.
boundaries: The NOT TENANTED pause is expected for a checkout job
happened: events 3-4: assigned the cleaner (Ava) and emailed the estimate request.

situation: The cleaner asks for the checkout report to be attached so she can quote.
happened: event 7: sent the checkout report to the cleaner.

situation: The cleaner says she uploaded the quote to the original request, but the agency cannot see it.
boundaries: The quote has not actually been received
happened: event 11: told the cleaner the quote had not attached.
note: The reply named the wrong property address (Flat 27, 117 Lantern Quay).

situation: The cleaning quote is now held, but the email asking the landlord for approval (event 13) went to the contractor by mistake.
boundaries: The landlord has not seen the quote yet, so do not chase him
happened: event 15: re-sent the quote to the landlord, asking whether to proceed with or without the carpets.

situation: The landlord says 'Yes please go ahead. Let them do the carpets too.'
boundaries: Approval covers the quoted clean including the carpets
happened: event 17: told the cleaner to proceed with the quote, including both bedroom carpets.
note: The agency asked for both bedroom carpets, while the quote mentioned bedroom two; any extra scope should match what was quoted and approved.

situation: The clean is done and the keys were returned ready for move-in on 30 Nov; no invoice has been received.
boundaries: No invoice has been received yet
happened: event 26: emailed the cleaner asking for the invoice.

situation: After the tenant vacated, the agency wants an estimate to replace a burnt carpet and repaint throughout.
boundaries: The tenant has vacated; do not route access through them
happened: events 3-5: assigned Cedar Utilities; template emails told the departed tenant and the contractor to arrange access with the tenant.
note: Sending the tenant-facing template to a vacated tenant was poor.

situation: Three automated reminders went unanswered, then the job sat on hold for about two weeks (25 Sep to 9 Oct) with no quote.
boundaries: No quote received yet
happened: no chase was sent; the quote arrived at event 12 on 9 Oct.
note: A good agent phones or emails the contractor directly, rather than leaving the job on silent hold.

situation: The contractor quoted: painting £220, carpet £240, bathroom vinyl £100, sink waste £45 (£605 in total).
boundaries: The landlord has not approved this quote
Vinyl and sink waste go beyond the original request (carpet and paint)
happened: event 13: sent the itemised quote to the landlord, asking to proceed.

situation: The landlord replied 'Pls go ahead' to the £605 quote.
boundaries: Approval covers the four quoted items only
happened: event 16: told the contractor the quote is approved and asked for start and completion dates.

situation: The contractor was instructed on 9 Oct and asked for start and completion dates; six days later there is no confirmation in the record.
boundaries: No start date confirmed
happened: event 18: an internal note says the contractor is attending this week.

situation: An internal note records the contractor completed the works; the contractor invoices the landlord directly.
boundaries: Completion is recorded only in an internal note; there are no photos or invoice
The landlord is invoiced directly; the agency has no invoice to forward
happened: events 21-27: marked complete, checked the keys were returned, and closed.

situation: The contractor quotes £198.37 plus VAT to replace two spotlights and one leak-damaged ceiling board found at checkout.
boundaries: The gate's 'landlord approval confirmed' covered getting a quote, not this price
happened: event 9: emailed the quote to the landlord asking whether the contractor may proceed.

situation: The landlord replied 'Pls go ahead' on 28 Sep; the system then paused the job as NOT TENANTED on 1 Oct.
boundaries: The NOT TENANTED pause is expected for an empty property
happened: events 16-17: told the contractor the quote is approved and asked when he can attend.
note: The agency took 3 days to instruct after approval.

situation: The contractor was instructed on 1 Oct and asked for an attendance date; there has been no reply for two days.
boundaries: No attendance date yet
happened: events 19-21: emailed and messaged the contractor asking when he can attend.

situation: The contractor offers to book Monday and asks where the keys are.
boundaries: The property is empty; access is by keys, not through a tenant
happened: event 25: told the contractor the keys are with the caretaker (4 days later).

situation: The contractor says 'we will get this in this week' after being told where the keys are.
boundaries: An acknowledgement is not completion
happened: event 29: sent a short 'Thank you!' and held.
note: Noise moment: nothing substantive to send.

situation: The contractor sent the invoice and photos for the completed job.
boundaries: Completion is evidenced by the contractor's invoice and photos only
happened: events 33-37: emailed the invoice to the landlord for payment and closed after checks.

situation: After the tenant vacated, the agency wants an estimate to repaint, replace the burnt bedroom carpet and the bathroom flooring, and repair a plug, a dripping tap and a shelf.
boundaries: A quote request is not approval of works
happened: events 2-4: assigned the provider and emailed the estimate request with the checkout report.

situation: The landlord received the first estimate and asked for a second contractor to quote for comparison.
boundaries: The landlord has approved neither quote
happened: events 10-11: noted the landlord wants a second quote and assigned a new provider.

situation: Both quotes were sent to the landlord on 2 May; there has been no reply for two days.
boundaries: No decision between the two quotes yet
happened: event 21: emailed the landlord asking for a decision on the two quotes.
note: The chase email listed unrelated property addresses, which is confusing.

situation: The landlord's reply is about roof work at another property and asks what was quoted; he has not decided between the quotes.
boundaries: A question about price is not approval
Roof works at another property are a separate job
happened: event 24: answered with both prices (Eliza Bennett £1,370; Kendall £1,700+VAT) and asked whether he wants the cheaper one.

situation: The landlord says 'Please go ahead with Eliza.'
boundaries: Approval is for Eliza Bennett's £1,370 quote, not Kendall's
happened: events 39-41: asked Eliza whether she will proceed, given the landlord's slow payment last time; she agreed.

situation: Eliza started the approved works around 26 May; a week later nothing has been heard.
boundaries: No completion confirmation or invoice yet
happened: events 42-45: marked complete, held for the invoice, then forwarded the invoice to the landlord, noting the tap was not replaced.

situation: After an inspection, the agency asked the tenant to sort the front garden and send photos; a week has passed with no reply.
boundaries: The garden is the tenant's responsibility here; no contractor is involved
happened: events 3-4: re-sent the request to the tenant (twice).

situation: The tenant has not replied to two written requests for photos of the front garden over 12 days.
boundaries: No evidence the garden has been done
happened: event 6: phoned the tenant, who said a family medical issue had delayed it and he would do it at the weekend.

situation: The tenant promised to do the garden at the weekend of 17-18 Feb and send a photo; nothing has arrived by 20 Feb.
boundaries: The tenant's promise is not evidence of completion
happened: event 9: emailed the tenant asking whether it was done and for photos.

situation: The tenant replied that the garden will be finished this evening and photos sent tomorrow morning.
boundaries: The tenant says it will be finished; no photo yet
happened: events 14-15: noted the reply and held.

situation: The tenant promised photos by 27 Feb; none have arrived by 1 Mar.
boundaries: No photo received; do not treat the garden as done
happened: events 16-17: emailed the tenant again (twice) asking for photos.
note: The chase emails named the wrong property address (Flat 2, 72 Lantern Quay).

situation: After a call about the tenant's emails not arriving, the agency confirmed the tenant's email with the photo has now come through.
boundaries: The photo is referenced but not visible in the record
happened: event 23: marked complete.

situation: A recurring task: get a solar panel meter reading photo from the tenant for the landlord every 3 months; the next one is due mid-June and it is November.
boundaries: The reading is not yet due
happened: event 2: held 'waiting for June'.

situation: The case has been on repeated holds 'waiting for mid June'; it is now 11 Jan.
boundaries: The due date in the record (mid-June) conflicts with asking now
happened: event 6: emailed the tenant asking for a clear photo of the solar readings.
note: Ambiguous: the request text says mid-June, but the agency asked in January and later labelled the photo 'for mid June'. The dates may be shifted.

situation: On a call on 13 Jan the tenant agreed to send the solar reading photo; four days later nothing has arrived.
boundaries: The tenant agreed to send it; nothing received yet
happened: event 10: re-sent the email request to the tenant.

situation: The tenant replied by email (the body is only a signature); the solar reading photo is attached.
boundaries: The tenant email has no text; the evidence is the attached photo
happened: event 13: forwarded the photo to the landlord and asked when the next reading is needed.

situation: The reading photo has been forwarded to the landlord, with a question about when the next one is due.
boundaries: The landlord has not yet confirmed the next due date
happened: event 14: marked done/complete; the landlord later replied that the next reading is due 15 Sept.

situation: Tenant reports the dishwasher never finishes its cycle (routine, two guinea pigs, no access issues); the system gate asks for landlord approval first.
boundaries: No landlord approval or standing consent is on file yet
Routine appliance fault; not an emergency that justifies attending without approval
happened: events 4-5: emailed landlord asking if a contractor may attend; system set a 3-day wait.

situation: Landlord asked for approval four days ago and has not replied; the system flagged no response after 3 days and simply re-armed the wait.
boundaries: Silence is not approval
happened: events 8-9: landlord replied 'Yes please go ahead' before any chase was sent.
note: No chase was sent after the 3-day flag; a chase was due, waiting one more day was borderline acceptable.

situation: Landlord has approved getting a contractor out to look at the dishwasher.
boundaries: Landlord approval to attend is not approval of any quote
happened: events 10-13: approval logged, Oakfield Homes assigned, tenant and contractor notified (about 2.5 days after the landlord replied).
note: The assignment was slow; it should have happened the day of the landlord reply.

situation: Contractor attended, removed water, tightened a loose heater connection and says it runs; a missing dial needs replacing for £95 inc VAT and they await go-ahead to order parts.
boundaries: Landlord approval to attend is not approval of the £95 dial quote
Contractor says it runs; tenant has not confirmed
happened: event 20: forwarded findings and the £95 quote to the landlord for approval.

situation: Landlord replied 'Please go ahead' to the £95 dial quote.
boundaries: Approval covers the quoted £95 dial only; any price increase needs fresh approval
happened: event 23: told the contractor to arrange the work.

situation: Contractor booked the dial job for 10 Dec and told the tenant they would fit the knob themselves; three days later there is no completion report or invoice on file.
boundaries: No completion report or invoice has been received yet
The tenant fitting the knob is a change of scope from the approved £95 job; confirm what is being billed
happened: events 26-32: moved to result, invoice uploaded (unavailable), closed after final checks with no visible landlord update.
note: Close-out had no visible completion evidence or landlord update; a good agent gets the completion report/invoice and confirms with the tenant before closing.

situation: Stale request 'dishwasher door not closing'; a note says the tenant never answered earlier troubleshooting and the link to the dishwasher was unclear.
boundaries: Do not assume the tenant's 'door won't close' refers to the dishwasher without confirming
happened: events 5-6: sent the tenant a troubleshooting checklist (twice).

situation: Tenant confirms all checks done and the dishwasher door still won't close; notes say the landlord already agreed to send an engineer.
boundaries: Landlord approval to inspect is not approval of any repair quote
happened: events 12-15: told landlord an engineer is instructed, assigned Riverside Compliance, notified tenant and contractor (2 days after tenant reply).

situation: Engineer attended on 29 Apr; four days later there are no work results and the system has flagged it.
boundaries: Contractor attended; no outcome or invoice reported yet
happened: event 24: invoice note arrived stating door lock freed and appliance tested working.

situation: Invoice note says the prematurely engaged door lock was fixed and the dishwasher tested working.
boundaries: Contractor says working; tenant has not confirmed
happened: events 25-31: moved to result and closed after final checks, no visible landlord message.
note: Informing the landlord of completion and invoice is the better close-out.

situation: Tenant reports the integrated dishwasher starts, beeps, flashes and stops; the system asks to approve provider and category.
boundaries: No landlord approval or standing consent is visible
happened: events 2-7: emailed the landlord that an engineer would be sent (notification, not a request) and assigned Harbour Surveying immediately.
note: The agency proceeded on notice alone; acceptable only with a standing consent not visible in the record. Asking for make/model or photos is also defensible.

situation: Contractor reached the tenant on 1 Oct and asked for model details, but three days on no appointment is confirmed.
boundaries: Contact with the tenant is not a booked appointment
happened: events 12-15: automated booking reminders to contractor on 4 and 5 Oct.

situation: Visit was booked for the morning of 8 Oct; three days later no work results have been received.
boundaries: Appointment booked is not evidence the repair happened
happened: event 26: put on hold 'waiting on response'.

situation: Contractor sent an invoice for the completed dishwasher job (£162.85).
boundaries: Invoice says completed; tenant has not confirmed the dishwasher works
happened: event 28: told landlord the dishwasher was repaired and the £162.85 invoice will come from rent.

situation: Repair invoiced, landlord informed, keys return confirmed; final checks done.
happened: event 34: request closed.

situation: Tenant and the fridge contractor report the front door must be slammed and the door and frame wobble, with a risk the glass may shatter.
boundaries: No landlord approval to attend yet
Routine unless the door fails to secure or glass breaks
happened: events 5-7: asked landlord whether someone can attend, acknowledged tenant, held for landlord.

situation: Landlord says it has happened before, suggests using the key to open the latch before closing, and offers a contractor next month.
boundaries: Landlord has deferred a contractor visit; this is not approval to attend now
happened: events 11-12: called tenant with the landlord's workaround; tenant had already tried it and it worked.

situation: Tenant says the key-latch workaround works and she will monitor and report any recurrence.
boundaries: Workaround, not a repair; the door fault remains
happened: events 13-15: told landlord the tenant is using the workaround and closed without payment.

situation: Tenant reports the front door sticks at the base with no obstruction; system asks to approve provider.
boundaries: No landlord approval on file
happened: events 3-5: asked landlord whether to instruct a contractor, updated tenant, held.

situation: Landlord replied asking that Imogen look at the door.
boundaries: Approval to inspect/fix is not approval of a large quote
happened: events 8-10: assigned provider, notified tenant and contractor.

situation: Contractor was assigned two days ago and sent the job with the tenant's contact; no update yet.
boundaries: No completion evidence yet
happened: event 15: contractor's invoice for £68.97 arrived.

situation: A £68.97 contractor invoice has arrived for the door job, but there is no completion report or tenant confirmation.
boundaries: Invoice is not a completion report; tenant has not confirmed
happened: event 16: told landlord the door was sorted, warning it is rotting and swelling and a replacement is recommended.
note: The landlord email named the wrong property address; the agent must use the case property.

situation: Landlord informed of the repair and the replacement recommendation; invoice added to the case.
boundaries: A door replacement is only a recommendation; landlord has not approved it
happened: event 18: completed by supervisor.

situation: Tenant reports the garden door is hard to close and creaks, hinges look misaligned, and gives availability; the gate asks for landlord approval.
boundaries: No landlord approval on file
happened: event 3: asked landlord whether to send a contractor or deal with it themselves.

situation: The landlord has not replied to the approval request for six days; the system flagged no response at day 3.
boundaries: Silence is not approval
happened: event 6: re-sent the approval request to the landlord.
note: The chase came 3 days after the system flag; it should have gone on day 3-4.

situation: Landlord (approval email had gone to spam) approves sending a contractor to check the door.
boundaries: Approval covers a simple fix; anything significant must be quoted first
happened: events 12-14: assigned Beacon Works with 'fix if simple, quote if expensive', notified tenant.

situation: Contractor assigned yesterday evening; no booking yet.
happened: events 15-19: contractor booked Friday 24 Oct 3pm; agency confirmed to both parties.

situation: Contractor reports the job complete, with no invoice because the door has settled naturally and works well.
boundaries: Contractor says door works; tenant has not confirmed
No invoice is due; do not chase one
happened: events 23-24: thanked contractor; told landlord (email typo says invoice 'was needed').

situation: Contractor confirmed no repair and no invoice needed; landlord informed.
happened: events 25-26: completed without payment.

situation: Tenant reports the kitchen extractor fan won't turn on; the gate asks for landlord approval.
boundaries: No landlord approval on file
happened: events 3-4: acknowledged tenant, asked landlord whether to use their own contractor or ours.
note: Asking the tenant to check the fan's isolator switch first would also be sensible.

situation: Landlord asked two days ago; only a 'Thank you!' acknowledgement from the tenant has arrived.
boundaries: Tenant's thank-you is acknowledgement only, not new information
happened: event 8: landlord replied that a switch to the right of the hob must be on.

situation: Landlord says there is a switch to the right of the hob that must be switched on.
boundaries: Landlord gave a troubleshooting tip, not approval for a contractor
happened: events 9-10: asked tenant to try the switch and report back.

situation: Tenant confirms the extractor works after finding the switch.
happened: events 12-14: told tenant the job will be closed; completed without payment.
note: The landlord was never told it was resolved; landlord.update is good close-out. Five-day delay before closing.

situation: Tenant says the garden is overgrown (tree, weeds) and in a communal area, too big to maintain; a gardener used to come yearly; the gate asks for landlord approval.
boundaries: Communal area may be the freeholder's or management company's, not the tenant's
No landlord approval is visible
happened: events 4-8: told tenant the gardener is on leave; system logged landlord approval (no landlord message visible); assigned Riverside Services.
note: Approval was logged with no visible landlord exchange, which may be a standing arrangement for the annual gardener.

situation: Three automated booking reminders went to the gardener over a week with no reply; the tenant was told the gardener is on annual leave.
boundaries: No booking confirmed
happened: events 12-13: system flagged reminders; next agency action was on 3 Jan telling the landlord the work was done.

situation: The gardener never confirmed a booking or a completion in the record; it is over two weeks since assignment.
boundaries: Nothing in the record shows the garden work was done
happened: event 13: told landlord the garden maintenance was done and would be invoiced off the rent.
note: The agency asserted completion with no visible evidence (probably known offline). A good agent gets confirmation first.

situation: Landlord acknowledged the completion message with thanks; no invoice is on file yet.
boundaries: Landlord's thanks is acknowledgement only
happened: events 16-17: invoice added and task completed by supervisor.

situation: Tenant asks for the garden to be cleared of rubbish and builders' waste, levelled and gravelled; the gate asks for landlord approval.
boundaries: Levelling and gravelling are improvements for the landlord to decide on, not a repair
happened: events 3-4: passed request to landlord, acknowledged tenant.

situation: Two weeks with no landlord reply; the system flagged no response on day 3.
boundaries: Silence is not approval
happened: events 8-9: notes say a new property manager is dealing with it and the landlord approved a £500+VAT quote.
note: No chase is visible for two weeks.

situation: Ten days after the agency sent the landlord a revised quote of about £600 for specialist waste removal, there is no reply.
boundaries: The earlier £500+VAT approval does not cover the revised quote
happened: event 22: chased the landlord for thoughts on the previous email.

situation: Landlord replies 'Please go ahead with the removal.'
boundaries: Approval covers waste removal only, not levelling or gravel
happened: event 26: asked Oakley to arrange the contractor.

situation: A note says the garden clearance was done and the agency is awaiting the contractor's invoice.
boundaries: No invoice on file yet
happened: event 33: contractor emailed the invoice (new provider, not on the portal).

situation: Garden cleared and invoice received for the landlord-approved removal.
boundaries: Tenant has not confirmed the clearance
happened: event 38: told landlord the garden was cleared, sent the invoice, deducting it from rent.

situation: Routine inspection booked for 13 Feb AM; tenant asks to move it to 'Friday 15th February' because of an excitable dog.
boundaries: 15 Feb 2024 is a Thursday; confirm the actual date
happened: events 7-12: spoke to tenant, rescheduled to 15 Feb PM and sent confirmation.

situation: Inspection done; the report rates all rooms Good but notes a tenant-installed dog flap in the back door and command-strip marks in Bedroom 1.
boundaries: Do not tell the landlord no issues were found when the report records an unapproved dog flap
Dog flap alteration is a landlord/tenant decision, not something to fix unilaterally
happened: events 17-18: sent landlord the report saying 'No issues were identified'.
note: The summary hid the dog flap; the landlord raised it himself later. Good practice is a landlord update that flags the alteration, or escalation.

situation: Inspection report sent to the landlord a day and a half ago; nothing outstanding from anyone.
happened: event 20: landlord replied raising the unapproved dog flap and the retrieval of a spare front door key after a lock change.

situation: Tenant reports the conservatory back-door key snapped with no spare; the system gate requires landlord approval first.
boundaries: Do not send a locksmith before the landlord approves
The agency holds no spare key for this door
happened: events 3-4: emailed landlord asking whether to send a contractor; system waits for reply.

situation: Landlord approved the lock work and asked for new keys for the tenant, landlord and agency.
boundaries: Brief must include the 4-key split: 2 tenant, 1 agency, 1 landlord, office keys dropped at the office
happened: events 7-12: thanked landlord, updated the task description with the key split, assigned Alder Compliance and notified the tenant.

situation: The contractor asks for the tenant's contact details to book the key replacement.
happened: event 16: sent the tenant's phone number to the contractor.

situation: Tenant contact details were given to the contractor about two hours earlier and no booking has been confirmed yet.
boundaries: Contact details sent only this morning; booking is not yet overdue
happened: event 18: automated booking reminder to contractor; contractor reported completion at event 20.
note: Waiting is the better call this soon after supplying contact details; the automated reminder is harmless.

situation: Contractor says the cylinder and handles are replaced and the remaining keys will be dropped at the office tomorrow.
boundaries: Contractor says done; tenant has not confirmed
Office and landlord keys have not been received yet
happened: events 21-29: thanked contractor, moved to result, and closed within minutes, marking 'keys return confirmed'.
note: The recorded close came before the promised key drop-off and with no tenant confirmation. A good agent updates the landlord and waits for the keys before closing.
